sentences.text: The Beaufort scale describes wind force by its effect on the sea.
Force three, a gentle breeze of seven to ten knots, brings scattered whitecaps.
Force four, a moderate breeze of eleven to sixteen knots, brings frequent whitecaps.
Force six, a strong breeze of twenty-two to twenty-seven knots, builds large waves with extensive foam crests, which is where many small charter boats stay at the dock.
Force eight is a gale, thirty-four to forty knots, and force twelve is hurricane force, sixty-four knots and above.
